physical.physical_description: Skirt cloth (Kain panjang) with a batik pattern on machine made tabby weave cotton cloth. The basic structure of the design consists of a ground with a loose  patchwork of traditional central Javanese designs. Superimposed on that background is a menagerie of wild animals and birds (elephants, leopards or tigers, deer, swan-like birds), a type of design known as kebun binatang or animal garden. The whole design direction is reversed half way through the cloth, making it technically a cloth of the type known as pagi-sore or morning-evening cloth.
physical.summary: Batik is the Indonesian name for the process of applying resist-dyed patterns to cloth. The principal places of manufacture are the areas around the Sultanates of Surakarta and Yogyakarta in central Java, some of the coastal towns of the north, such as Cirebon, Lasem, Pekalongan and Indramayu, and the area around Garut in western Java. The traditional batiks from the manufacturing centres in central Java are distinct from those in the other areas and typically show a restrained range of colours--rich browns, indigo blue, cream, white and black being the main elements of the palette. This batik, which is in the form of a kain panjang, or man's skirt cloth, has all the hallmarks of a central Javanese example, including a loose patchwork background of traditional central Javanese designs. Superimposed on that is a menagerie of wild animals and birds (elephants, leopards or tigers, deer, swanlike birds)--a type of design known as kebun binatang or animal garden. Further, the whole design direction is reversed half way through the cloth, making it technically a cloth of the type known as pagi-sore--a cloth that can be reversed for wearing either in the morning or the evening.
